text:
samir: FYI — prototyping a transport toggle for console streams: internal gRPC bidi vs HTTP/2 SSE over the gateway for browser clients. Idea is per-route transport config so we can optimize latency/cost independently. Thoughts?

maya: SSE is simplest for the console, works with fetch/eventsource and avoids gRPC-web shims in the UI. But need a gateway translator if we keep internal gRPC.

alex: gRPC-web + envoy is fine but ops config gets annoying. Also grpc-web limits some bidi semantics — we usually fake it with client streaming.

jamie: important: quota and tenant routing headers must propagate. We can't lose X-Quota-Tier or x-tenant-id during translation. Example header we rely on: `X-Quota-Tier: premium`

infra-bot: heads-up: SSE opens a long-lived connection per tab. At 100k active users that is a lot of sockets. Suggest multiplexing streams or using a single websocket per user and multiplex topics.

ops-bot: deploybot: triggered canary for `transport-toggle` spike on staging. 2 hosts, 5% traffic. ETA 14:00 PT. :rocket:

maya: also UI/UX: rollouts page needs to display active transport and fallback state (e.g., "gRPC internal → SSE fallback"). Devs should be able to flip transport per-route without redeploying model.

samir: agree re: fallback display. For telemetry we should attach route metadata to traces and metrics: span.attr route.name, transport=grpc|sse, translator=envoy-proxy if used. Sampling rules?

alex: sample all errors + 0.1% of success streams. Also surface connection churn metric: `stream_conn_restarts` and `avg_keepalive_ms`.

jamie: scale/cost note: continuous full-state streams can be heavy. Recommend delta encoding (send diffs) and batched updates. Example payload suggestion:

```
{ "route": "inference.v1/predict", "deltas": [{"q": "premium", "tokens": 123}], "ts": 1650000000 }
```

samir: good point. Deltas + sparse heartbeat will cut cost. Also consider per-tenant backpressure: if client lagging, drop non-critical updates.

infra-bot: for internal gRPC route we can reuse our existing xDS config, but note that translating gRPC->SSE means per-request buffering at gateway — increases memory pressure.

maya: question: do we keep a single canonical transport internally (grpc), and only translate at the edge? Or do we let services publish both SSE and grpc endpoints and let the router choose?

alex: my vote: canonical internal gRPC stream for service-to-service. Gateway does on-the-fly translation to SSE/websocket for browsers. That keeps internal telemetry consistent and keeps service code simple.

jamie: OK as long as gateway preserves quota headers and auth principal. We need an integration test matrix: auth flow, quota enforcement, and downgrade to polling.

samir: action items: 1) I'll spike gRPC internal + envoy translator to SSE on staging (samir -> will push branch). 2) Maya, can you mock UI toggle and fallback indicator? 3) Jamie, can you add quota-header e2e tests to the routing suite? ops-bot will schedule the canary at 14:00.

maya: yes I can mock. Will add transport column to rollouts table.

jamie: adding tests now. low-fi will run in CI.

ops-bot: deploybot: canary started. watch `transport-toggle-staging` dashboard.

samir: thanks all — keeping this lightweight for the spike. If we see connection churn or memory pressure we'll pivot to multiplexed websocket. :thumbsup:

alex: +1. Please log perf numbers (p95 connect latency, memory delta) in the canary thread.

infra-bot: note: add `x-route-id` to span tags to make it trivial to slice telemetry by the transport.

samir: noted. will include `x-route-id`.

maya: one more UX ask — show "transport: experimental" badge for routes using the new toggle so product doesn't rely on it yet.

samir: makes sense. delaying GA until we have perf + e2e.

jamie: :white_check_mark: done with tests, opening PR.

samir: closing loop later today after canary results. Thanks everyone :)
